notes.summary: A convex chord lemma proves every joint index/time recession limit from fixed-time liminf recovery and matching finite slopes. An infinite-slope variant requires no approximant slope convergence. Neither proves fixed-time equality or a uniform additive remainder.
notes.detailedSummary: For finite convex f_j and f with f_j(0)→f(0)=a, liminf_j f_j(T)≥f(T) at each T>0, and finite recession slopes ℓ_j→ℓ=f∞, one has f_j(t_j)/t_j→ℓ for every joint index/time sequence. The proof sandwiches the quotient between a fixed-time chord and its recession slope. If the extended convex target has recession +∞, the lower bound alone gives joint divergence, including when a finite-time target value is infinite. These are scalar mathematical lemmas, not analytic counterexamples to P19.2.
notes.text:
Finite recession lemma. Let f_j:[0,∞)→R be finite convex, f_j(0)→a∈R, and f:[0,∞)→R be finite convex with f(0)=a. Assume liminf_j f_j(T)≥f(T) for every T>0, and ℓ_j:=lim_{t→∞}f_j(t)/t→ℓ:=lim_{t→∞}f(t)/t∈R. Then f_j(t_j)/t_j→ℓ whenever the index tends to infinity and t_j→∞.

Proof. Convexity makes (f_j(t)−f_j(0))/t nondecreasing, with limit ℓ_j. For t≥T>0,
 f_j(0)/t+(f_j(T)−f_j(0))/T ≤ f_j(t)/t ≤ f_j(0)/t+ℓ_j.
Along any joint sequence the upper bound tends to ℓ, while the lower bound has liminf at least (f(T)−a)/T. Let T→∞. The bounds coincide. The argument applies to arbitrary subsequences of indices and therefore proves the full joint quantifier.

Infinite recession lemma. Keep f_j finite convex with f_j(0)→a, and allow an extended convex target f:[0,∞)→R∪{+∞}, with f(0)=a and recession +∞. Assume the same fixed-time liminf inequality. The lower chord bound proves f_j(t_j)/t_j→+∞ without any condition on the approximant recession slopes. If f(T)=+∞ at some fixed T, the lower bound already forces divergence. Otherwise choose large T with (f(T)−a)/T arbitrarily large, take the joint liminf first, then increase T.

The limitations are exact. Take f(t)=2t−min(t,1) and every f_j(t)=2t. Both are convex, start at zero, have recession 2, and satisfy the required liminf inequality, yet their gap at t=1 is one. For f_k(t)=2t−min(t/k,k), the target is 2t and 0≤2−f_k(t)/t≤1/k, but lim_{t→∞}(f_k(t)−2t)=−k. Thus no uniform additive O(1) remainder follows. These examples are scalar implication diagnostics only.

notes.text:
Theorem and conventions. Let X be connected smooth compact Kähler, dim X=n≥1, ω Kähler, α=[ω], V=∫ω^n and μ0=ω^n/V. Set dd^c=(i/2π)∂∂bar and t=−log|τ|². Use E(u)=((n+1)V)^−1 Σ_{k=0}^n∫u⟨ω_u^k⟩∧ω^{n−k}, MA(u)=V^−1⟨ω_u^n⟩ and full probability entropy H(u)=Ent(MA(u)|μ0). Keep the actual prescribed w∈E1 with H(w)<∞ exactly; w may be unbounded and nonmodel. Actual weak rays are strongly continuous at zero and canonical finite-energy geodesics on every finite interval.

Suppose ψ_j→ψ strongly in E^{1,NA}(α), every Hα(ψ_j)<∞, and put r_j=r(w,ψ_j), r=r(w,ψ). If Hα(ψ)<∞ and Hα(ψ_j)→Hα(ψ), then H(r_j,t_j)/t_j→Hα(ψ) for every joint index/time sequence. If Hα(ψ)=+∞, these ratios tend to +∞ without an additional condition on the approximant entropy limit. In both branches (E(r_j,t_j)−E(w))/t_j=Eα(ψ_j)→Eα(ψ), and the rays converge in d1 uniformly on bounded time intervals.

Exact caller premises. R grants actual maximal rays from every w∈E1, their usual datum, order, affine energy, bounded-time continuity under strong NA convergence, calibrated finite contracted-energy slopes strongly continuous in the datum, its entropy classification, finite-time entropy when initial and NA entropy are finite, and actual relatively Kähler model recovery with converging NA entropy for finite-entropy targets. Its complete body is the premise; historical verdicts are not. T, C and S retain only their stated curve, CPn, relative-envelope and model scopes. No grant supplies general closed P-profile density or nonmaximal approximation.

Actual models and carrier. Retain the original full X^beth, including supported semivaluations. The usual datum comes from generic divisorial coefficients of the actual total potential, not division of a pointwise −∞ value by time. On a smooth equivariant modification ρ:Y→X×P1, a vertical real D gives the relatively Kähler cohomological model A=ρ_X*α+[D], with f_D(v_F)=D_F/b_F and b_F=ord_F(τ). Compatibility has sign U+log|s_D|²=O(1) for bounded model weights. Its probability measure is V^−1Σ_F b_F(A^n·F)δ_{v_F}; Eα(f_D)=A^{n+1}/((n+1)V), with R's trivialization near infinity. Hα(ψ)=∫A_X MAα(ψ), and the central SNC discrepancy factor is (κ_F+1−b_F)/b_F. Neither multiplicities nor supports are removed. General transcendental classes use real cohomological models; no rational line bundle or semiampleness is presumed.

New primary application. Berman–Darvas–Lu, Geometry & Topology 21 (2017), 2945–2988, DOI 10.2140/gt.2017.21.2945, primary PDF https://msp.org/gt/2017/21-5/gt-v21-n5-p08-s.pdf: Proposition 4.4 gives d1 continuity of contracted energy for smooth closed real forms on E1. Proposition 4.5 gives convexity for smooth positive forms on bounded-Laplacian weak geodesics. Theorem 4.7 at twist zero and p=1 gives lower semicontinuity and convexity of extended Mabuchi. Complete statement/proof layout units 1852–1938, 2004–2085 and 2165–2307 were read and retained; defining conventions and twist condition were checked. Extend contracted-energy convexity to E1 segments by decreasing smooth endpoints, the granted R decreasing-geodesic foundations, and Proposition 4.4, then pass to the limit in the convexity inequalities. The bounded source theorem is not silently applied to singular endpoints.

Normalization. The source uses i∂∂bar. Its potential v=u/(2π), with the same ω, gives our current and probability measure. Its d1 is our d1/(2π), AM(v)=E(u)/(2π), and Tγ(u)=2πn AMγ(v), where Tγ(u)=V^−1Σ_{k=0}^{n−1}∫uγ∧⟨ω_u^k⟩∧ω^{n−1−k}. Its Ricci form and mean scalar are 2π times ours. Its untwisted K(v) is consequently exactly M(u)=H(u)+G(u), with G=T_{−Ric(ω)}+Sbar E, Ric(ω)=−dd^c logω^n and Sbar=nV^−1∫Ric(ω)∧ω^{n−1}. Entropy's coefficient remains one.

Joint correction proof. For positive smooth closed γ, Tγ(r_j,t) is finite convex. At fixed T, bounded-time d1 recovery and contracted-energy continuity give Tγ(r_j,T)→Tγ(r_T). Initial values equal Tγ(w). R supplies finite recession slopes Lγ(ψ_j)→Lγ(ψ); on models Lγ(f_D)=V^−1 A^n·ρ_X*[γ]. Apply n1 to obtain Tγ(r_j,t_j)/t_j→Lγ(ψ). For signed γ, choose a fixed c with γ+cω≥0 and subtract the two positive-form conclusions. Affine energy then gives G(r_j,t_j)/t_j→Gα(ψ), a finite limit. No uniform time-dependent mixed-pairing estimate is required.

Entropy proof. Each f_j(t)=M(r_j,t) is finite convex, starts at the fixed finite M(w), and has recession m_j=Hα(ψ_j)+Gα(ψ_j). At fixed T, lower semicontinuity gives M(r_T)≤liminf_j M(r_j,T). In the finite branch the target has finite-time values and recession m=Hα(ψ)+Gα(ψ), with m_j→m. Apply n1's finite lemma and subtract the independent joint correction limit. In the infinite branch the target Mabuchi recession is +∞; finite-time target values may be infinite. Apply n1's infinite lemma, then subtract the finite correction. This proves both joint entropy conclusions.

Model corollary. For finite Hα(ψ), take the actual relatively Kähler model data η_j from R equation (16), strongly convergent with NA entropy recovery. Apply the theorem to r(w,η_j), retaining the identical w. No projectivity assumption is introduced. This strengthens S Section 5's general maximal recovery by proving its joint entropy conclusion. It gives no fixed-time entropy continuity, closed relative P-profile construction or arbitrary nonmaximal-ray approximation.
